jcr:title: Mako Partial Knee SmartRobotics™
jcr:description: Mako Partial Knee enables surgeons to create a 3D CT-based surgery plan of their patient's unique anatomy.

text.text:
Know more. Cut less.5,6

 

Know more. Mako Partial Knee's 3D CT-based plan allows you to plan for each patient’s unique anatomy, so you know more.

Additionally, Mako Partial Knee helps enable surgeons to dynamically balance soft tissue tensioning intraoperatively, with the goal of recreating natural knee kinematics. 

Cut less.5,6 Using AccuStop™ haptic technology and everything the CT scan helps you to know about your patient, you are no longer limited by cutting blocks and manual techniques. AccuStop™ haptic technology creates a virtual boundary that assists you in executing both the tibial and femoral bone resections to plan. So you can cut less.

text.text:
Mako Partial Knee features
dynamic joint balancing

 

  • Mako Partial Knee helps enable the surgeon to dynamically balance soft tissue tensioning intraoperatively, with the goal of recreating natural knee kinematics.
  • Studies have shown that Mako Partial Knee has the potential to:
    • Reproducibly deliver component placement that is accurate to the 3D patient-specific preoperative plans1,2 
    • Reduce damage to the surrounding soft tissue through AccuStop™ haptic technology, based on a cadaveric study3
    • Help surgeons reestablish soft tissue balance using dynamic joint balancing4

text_711672110.text: Not all robotics are the same.

text_1799716854.text:
Mako Partial Knee

shows 46% reduction in risk of revision.7

 

In the Australian Orthopaedic Association National Joint Replacement Registry 2025 Annual Report the Restoris MCK implanted with Mako Partial Knee shows a 46% reduction in risk of revision over nine years when compared to aggregated Other Unicompartmental Knees*7 

(Hazard Ratio, adjusted for age and gender Restoris MCK/Restoris MCK vs Other Unicompartmental Knee. Entire Period: HR=0.54 (0.49, 0.60),p<0.001). 

 

 

*Which includes all unicompartmental knee procedures, including those with technology assistance, computer navigation and no technology assistance combined.

experiencefragment.text: Over 10 years of clinical success At a mean follow-up of 11.1 years, patients who underwent medial partial knee arthroplasty displayed the following: Survivorship rate of 96.4%8 4.4 out of 5 satisfied or very satisfied8 Excellent Forgotten Joint Score of 82.28 88.8% of patients achieved Patient Acceptable Symptoms State8

text.text: In clinical studies, Mako Partial Knee has demonstrated:

Greater precision to plan

Multiple studies of Mako Partial Knees have demonstrated improved accuracy of component position when compared to manually implanted partial knees.1,9

text_copy.text:
Improved outcomes

Studies comparing Mako Partial Knee to both manual and total knee surgeries have shown improvements in objective and subjective functional outcomes.10,12-14

Reduced risk of revision

Registry data reports 45% lower risk of revision for the Restoris MCK compared to aggregated ‘Other Unicompartmental Knee*’ (Hazard Ratio=0.55 (0.49, 0.61),p<0.001)7

text.text:
Less pain 

Multiple studies have demonstrated a significant reduction in postoperative pain with Mako Partial Knees when compared to manual partial knees.10,11

text_copy.text:
Shorter length of hospital stay 

A study found Mako Partial Knee was associated with a 40.2% reduction in time to discharge compared to manual partial knee, averaging 28 hours faster (42.5 vs. 71.1 hours, p<0.001).10

text_copy_1076750929.text:
High ten-year survival rates

Studies report ten-year survival rates between 93% - 100% 8,15-16

text_1849202346_copy.text: Restoris MCK partial knee implant

text_copy.text:
The Restoris MCK partial knee implant system, used with Mako Partial Knee, is designed from over 100 CT scans to fit a broad spectrum of knee anatomies across different sizes and genders.5 The combination supports the restoration of native knee kinematics and aims to enhance patient outcomes.11,17,18


Bone-sparing, curved design

The implant designs feature bone-sparing, curved surfaces enabled by Mako robotic-arm assistance allowing surgeons to create anatomic, sculpted resections using either the burr-only or planar workflow for bone preparation.5 

 

Targeted solutions for multiple disease states

Restoris MCK offers a solution for patients suffering from osteoarthritis in one or more compartments of the knee: medial unicompartmental, lateral unicompartmental, patellofemoral and medial bicompartmental.

pageshortdescription.shortDescTitle: The outcomes you can achieve have the potential to create the future of your orthopaedic service line.
pageshortdescription.shortDescTop:
While partial knee replacement accounts for less than 10% of all knee arthroplasty performed, studies have indicated the incidence could be 20% or more depending on timing of surgery with the disease process.1

 

Mako Partial Knee Technology facilitates enhanced precision2,3 and enables you to perform technically challenging partial knee procedures.
